data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are clearly attached at the same node, visible in close-up images, with 3-4 leaves per node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at nodes, forming whorled clusters along the stem)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly rounded, not tapered or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off and curving toward margins)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, spaced widely, 4-6 pairs per leaf (secondary veins are prominent, arching from midrib to margin, with noticeable spacing)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull, glabrous (surface is smooth and not shiny, with no visible hairs)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible surface hairs or fuzz)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are short, less than 1 cm, connecting leaf blade to stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles are round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem is firm, greenish-brown, with visible bark texture, typical of young woody plants)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: greenish-brown (stem has a greenish-brown hue, with some mottling and slight moss in background, but stem itself is primarily greenish-brown)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf bases or nodes)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible when stems or leaves are broken)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus visible at leaf bases; not applicable as leaf arrangement is whorled, not typical of Fabaceae)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: The seedling displays whorled, simple, elliptic leaves with entire margins and pinnate venation. New leaves emerging are reddish, indicating young growth. Some leaves show minor damage (small holes, discoloration, and spots), but these are not clearly linked to herbivory or pathogens. The stem is woody and smooth, with no visible trichomes or latex. The leaf arrangement and morphology are consistent across all images, with no conflicting observations. The surrounding forest floor is littered with decomposing leaves, but no habitat inferences are made.
